articles.title: The 'low hire, low fire' job market could finally crack in 2027
articles.summary: Here are the top three job market trends to watch for in 2027, according to a new report.
articles.body:
Amid a long-running 'low hire, low fire' job market, new research suggests workers are on the cusp of an inflection year where job hopping comes roaring back.

Here are the top three trends to watch for in 2027, according to a new report from Indeed Hiring Lab and Glassdoor Economic Research.

Workers' pent-up frustration over feeling stuck in their job could quickly shift. Rising job postings and upbeat hiring managers point to a rebound that could unleash turnover.

"After years of very little movement, several metros are starting to turn the corner," Laura Ullrich, director of economic research at the Indeed Hiring Lab, told Yahoo Finance. "Job postings are now above pre-pandemic levels in more than three-quarters of major metros.

"It's too early to call it a recovery, but more local markets moving in the right direction is an encouraging sign heading into 2027."

This year, the job market "kept a lot of unhappy workers right where they were," said Daniel Zhao, Glassdoor's chief economist.

For the most part, unemployment has been low, wages generally flat and trailing inflation, pushing people to hold on to their jobs whether they like them or not.

Where were they going to go anyway? For three years, hiring has been stagnant. "They want out, but the market hasn't given them the opportunities to leave," he said. "When people are frustrated with their career prospects, we'd normally expect to see more of them quit, and 2027 could be the year that finally happens"

If hiring picks back up, employees who stayed put this year may be the first ones out the door, he added. But a job jump might be to a different industry, not just a new employer.

Most local markets are warming back up on the hiring front. Job postings are above pre-pandemic levels in 299 of 385 US metros analyzed in this report.

Postings for software development, banking and finance, and engineering have seen recent growth. If this trend continues, you can expect more hiring in some of these previously soft white-collar sectors, Zhao said. Many of the gains are modest, but the direction is consistent.

The share of metros with year-over-year job posting growth jumped from 10% at the start of 2026 to almost half by September. That's the biggest jump since late 2022.

The hitch is that it's not being felt across the board. Senior-level postings are up, while entry- and mid-level postings have each dropped, and that trend is expected to continue.

articles.title: Aging means learning how to prevent costly scams targeting older Americans
articles.summary: FTC reports fraud targeting older adults could have cost up to $119.5 billion last year, with romance and impersonation scams among top threats.
articles.body: Getting older comes with some unpleasant consequences — aches and pains, worsening vision and even some forgetfulness. But one of the downsides of aging that isn’t discussed enough is that it also puts you at a higher risk of being targeted by scammers and losing money to fraud and scams. A recent report by the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to Congress stated that the cost of consumer fraud targeting older adults (60 and older) could have been as high as $119.5 billion last year. Plus, the risk of higher median losses also occurred with older adults, with a large disparity for those 80 years old and older. When it comes to preying on older adults, scammers come from far and wide. The types of schemes and scams are varied, from romance schemes to tech support scams to fake sweepstakes and lotteries, investment scams and all kinds of impersonation scams, whether the scammer is impersonating a financial institution, government personnel or even a family member. MEDICARE AND SOCIAL SECURITY SCAMS: WARNING SIGNS AND TIPS Experts say that there are very concrete reasons that scammers focus on the aging population. Some of those have to do with having lived for decades in a high-trust society, which takes people at their word and generates a culture of being polite and even obedient to authority. Another reason is that, in the U.S., more wealth has accumulated with the older generations, so the scammers are just following the money. DATA BROKER OPT-OUT: HOW RETIREES CAN PROTECT THEIR DATA Other factors include preying on loneliness, exploiting cognitive issues and even a lack of familiarity with technology. So, given that scammers are trying to manipulate and scam those who are aging, how can you protect yourself or your aging family members from these schemes? CYBERCRIME LOSSES NEAR $21B: 5 WAYS TO PROTECT YOUR MONEY One of my late father’s favorite sayings was, "If it sounds too good to be true, it is." This is a great mantra to remember when it comes to scams. If a young, gorgeous person approaches you for a romantic liaison, be careful, and if they ask you to send them money, you can feel confident that it is a scam. If an investment is promising an outsized return, it’s also likely a scam. Be on high alert for any "luck" that seems to have befallen you and consider consulting some trusted sources for a second and third opinion before making any decisions on these special "offers." Building on my dad’s mantra, I have created my own — if it sounds weird, it probably is. Details that don’t add up in the real world are a red flag. You are not James Bond, and therefore, you should not be asked to do anything that puts you in the middle of a spy thriller plot. This includes working with government officials, police, the FBI, major companies like Amazon or financial institutions to catch a criminal. None of the above would ever ask a citizen to do that. And, if you are told you need to keep a secret because someone in an authority position may be in on the plot, that is Hollywood writing, not reality! FAKE FEDERAL AGENTS PUSH SENIORS TO TURN SAVINGS INTO GOLD BARS FOR COURIERS TO COLLECT The same mantra applies to someone instructing you to move money to be "safe" or directing you to change your funds into another form of currency, whether that be gift cards, cryptocurrency or something else. No legitimate law enforcement, financial services or other entities need your help to catch criminals, and if your own accounts were actually at risk, no one should or will ask you to undertake spy-level activities. Again, consider consulting some outside sources, including trusted family members or authorities, before you take any action. Another tactic to keep scammers at bay is to defuse their urgency. Creating urgency is key for scammers. They make you worried and that causes you to panic. You can defuse the urgency by not picking up calls you aren’t expecting and not replying to any urgent calls to action. articles.body: BENGALURU: India’s The ePlane Company has selected US-based Lynx Software Technologies’ “LYNX MOSA.ic platform” to run multiple software systems on its e200X electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft, enabling safety-critical and mission-specific applications to operate on shared computing modules without interfering with each other.Announced at the eVTOL Show USA on Nov 18, the partnership will see the software platform used for mission computing aboard the e200X, a three-seat aircraft (one pilot and two passengers) being developed for air ambulance, urban cargo and passenger services.The aircraft has a modular airframe, with different configurations carrying varying payloads, sensor systems and software requirements. However, flight control systems need to remain deterministic and certifiable across all configurations.LYNX MOSA.ic addresses this through a partitioned computing architecture. Flight-critical applications, including vehicle and energy management systems, will operate in dedicated ARINC 653 partitions, isolated from lower-criticality functions such as sensor data processing and enhanced situational awareness.Heavy artificial intelligence processing will run on a separate platform, with the mission system providing controlled interfaces between it and the rest of the aircraft. This separation is intended to maintain safety and cybersecurity boundaries while allowing mission-specific software to evolve.The platform is built around a separation kernel-based Type 1 hypervisor, which assigns individual software applications dedicated space and time partitions. It is certifiable to DO-178C Design Assurance Level A, a standard for safety-critical airborne software.Prof Satya Chakravarthy, founder and technical lead of The ePlane Company, said the technology would allow the company to isolate safety-critical systems while developing additional aircraft functionalities.Founded in 2019 and incubated at the Indian Institute of Technology Madras, ePlane is developing the e200X as a multi-role electric aircraft. articles.title: The Bank of Nvidia's tab jumped to nearly $670 billion — and its customers are taking longer to pay: Chart of the Day
articles.summary: Nvidia's lending and supply promises grew by nearly $140 billion in Jensen Huang's final quarter as CEO.
articles.body:
Jensen Huang started reining in the Bank of Nvidia months before he left. It got bigger anyway.

Third quarter results from Nvidia ( NVDA ) on Tuesday covered the last quarter during which Huang served as CEO. They also updated the number investors have watched since his exit put the company's web of AI deals under the microscope.

Everything Nvidia has promised to buy, back, or invest now comes to nearly $670 billion, up from about $530 billion in July, by Yahoo Finance calculations.

Most of the jump is for chips, not loans. Promises to suppliers swelled to $390 billion from $279 billion, mostly to lock up memory for years to come.

The riskier piece is the backstops. Nvidia carries $118 billion in guarantees — promises to pay if a partner can't — including nearly $10 billion in new ones for partners it didn't name. It says it hasn't paid out on any of them.

"Neoclouds and frontier labs are seeing extraordinary demand for AI infrastructure, yet many are growing faster than their balance sheets and long-term credit profiles can support," interim CEO Colette Kress wrote in her commentary on the quarter .

New pledges did shrink, to $32 billion for neoclouds — cloud companies that rent out Nvidia's chips — and $20 billion for investments in other companies.

But the checks kept coming. Nvidia bought nearly $16 billion of stakes in other companies in the quarter, mostly private ones it didn't name. Among public companies, its latest holdings filing shows it added to SpaceX ( SPCX ) while trimming Intel ( INTC ) and Nokia ( NOK ). So far this fiscal year, those purchases have eaten up nearly half of the cash its business generated, according to Yahoo Finance calculations.

Nvidia's accounts receivable — bills sent but not yet paid — hit $81 billion, or 64 days of sales. That's the most since the 2022 chip slump by a measure called days sales outstanding .

Nvidia pointed to "extended payment terms on large, multi-quarter agreements with certain investment-grade customers." In other words, some of its biggest buyers are getting more time to pay.

The full books will have to wait. Nvidia said its 10-Q quarterly report would come "in the coming weeks," not the same evening as usual. Its release also mentioned an ongoing investigation by an independent board committee.

"The deep financing arm of Nvidia is ... a moat that no competitor is ... going to be able to get close to anytime soon," Patrick Moorhead, founder and CEO of Moor Insights & Strategy, told Yahoo Finance last week.

articles.title: Inside the major shake-up coming to House Financial Services Committee
articles.summary: The House Financial Services Committee is due for a shake-up come January, as Democrats will be in the majority on a panel set to feature multiple new GOP members. That will usher in multiple changes for the committee, from a different set of priorities to potentially a new name. With the party’s House leadership elections…
articles.body:
The House Financial Services Committee is due for a shake-up come January, as Democrats will be in the majority on a panel set to feature multiple new GOP members.

That will usher in multiple changes for the committee, from a different set of priorities to potentially a new name.

With the party’s House leadership elections set for Wednesday and Thursday , two Democrats are fighting for the gavel: Reps. Maxine Waters (Calif.), the top Democrat on the panel since 2013, and Sean Casten (D-Ill.).

Casten, a member of the committee since he entered the House in January 2019 and the vice ranking member, launched his leadership bid on Nov. 5.

A day later, Waters confirmed she was seeking the gavel again. The California Democrat spent the 116th and 117th Congresses chairing the panel, which oversees Wall Street , the Federal Reserve and the Treasury and Housing and Urban Development departments.

In letters to their colleagues, both lawmakers outlined similar priorities should they succeed Rep. French Hill (R-Ark.) as House Financial Services chair.

The two vowed to support legislation that would boost the country’s affordable housing supply, crack down on President Trump’s sprawling business interests and establish regulatory frameworks for cryptocurrency and prediction markets .

“We need to lower housing and insurance costs, protect consumers from fraud, scams, and the risks posed by crypto and prediction markets, and secure the financial system from the next crisis,” wrote Casten, 54.

Similarly, the 88-year-old Waters wrote the panel must “address the crushing affordability crisis, expand access to housing, foster a dynamic and fair financial system, and hold the corrupt Trump Administration accountable.”

Waters also previewed her oversight crackdown this week, as she instructed officials at the Fed, Treasury and more than 20 other federal agencies to preserve documents and communications dating to Trump’s first day back in office.

Differences between Waters and Casten, though, have recently emerged. Casten told Punchbowl News last Thursday the panel has had “far too much churn” on the Democratic side — five members who served on the committee during the 117th Congress and are still in office are no longer members.

“That troubles me a little bit,” the Illinois Democrat said, before pointing out that it took five months for Rep. Everton Blair (D-Ga.) to replace the late Rep. David Scott (D-Ga.), who died in April , on the panel.

“This is an A committee,” he added. “Why didn’t we have someone who wanted to be in that spot?”

Waters then lobbed personal attacks at Casten, saying her deputy “misled” her on whether he was going to challenge her leadership position for the next Congress.

“I was surprised. Disappointed. And now, I believe he’s not trustworthy,” the Capitol Hill veteran told Punchbowl on Friday.

Waters has the edge among her Democratic colleagues. The broader Congressional Black Caucus (CBC), along with seven CBC members who serve on the Financial Services panel, backed her gavel bid last month, Politico reported .

The same goes for five members of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus who serve on the panel. In a letter to their colleagues shared with The Hill, the lawmakers wrote Waters “knows how to continue delivering” results.

“As we continue to face an affordability crisis, her expertise and experience make Congresswoman Waters uniquely suited to lead the Committee through the challenges currently facing our economy and financial system,” they wrote.

Waters additionally has the support of the National Fair Housing Alliance, which backed her bid for chair after Democrats swept to control of the House and Senate in the midterm elections .

The California Democrat worked with Hill to pass the bipartisan 21st Century Road to Housing Act, which took effect over the summer without Trump’s signature and seeks to streamline federal review processes for new unit construction.

Waters was clear in her letter earlier this month about how she would put “housing first.” She even said she plans on renaming the panel to the “Committee on Housing and Financial Services” if elected chair.

Second-term Rep. Brittany Pettersen (D-Colo.) is also backing Waters. The Colorado Democrat told The Hill last Wednesday her colleague has “an incredible team” and “aligned” priorities.

“My understanding is I don’t know if she’s going to be doing this to another term, but I think that she deserves the opportunity in the majority,” Pettersen added.

As for what Waters should focus on if she leads the committee for another two years, Pettersen highlighted the “housing crisis,” cracking down on corruption and restoring funding for the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, which the Trump administration has sought to dismantle .

But another Democrat on the committee, Rep. Jim Himes (Conn.), was tight-lipped about the Waters-Casten battle. The Connecticut Democrat, who has served on the panel since he entered Congress in 2009, told The Hill last week he is “not commenting on that race.”

Whether Waters or Casten holds the gavel in 2027, the next Financial Services chair will lead a committee that features a slew of new members in the minority.

Of the 30 Republicans on the committee, 14 will not be in the 120th Congress. The reasons vary — Reps. Bill Huizenga (R-Mich.), Mike Lawler (R-N.Y.) and Bryan Steil (R-Wis.) are among seven GOP members who lost their reelection bids earlier this month .

Rep. Byron Donalds (R-Fla.), meanwhile, is on his way to the Florida governor’s mansion, and Rep. Andy Barr (R-Ky.) is headed to the Senate.

The Republican turnover nearly extended to Hill, who won his race against Democrat Chris Jones by less than 2 percentage points . Two years ago, Hill won reelection by nearly 18 points.

Former Rep. Patrick McHenry (R-N.C.), the top Republican on the panel from 2019 to 2023, told Bloomberg earlier this month the election was “brutal” for his former GOP colleagues.

“Many of them have had the long-tested major battleground districts like a Bryan Steil and [Rep. Ann] Wagner (R-Mo.), but many of them were in solid Republican districts, like [Rep.] Tim Moore (R-N.C.),” added McHenry, who served as acting Speaker for roughly three weeks in October 2023.

While it is unclear which members will fill the gaps, Hill recently outlined his approach to being in the minority. The Arkansas Republican told KARK-TV in Little Rock he wants to collaborate with Democrats on common “priorities,” including the implementation of the housing law.

“I’m hoping my Democratic colleagues and I, on both sides of the Capitol, can make sure that Secretary [Scott] Turner at HUD and the other bank regulators and others get this fully implemented,” Hill told Caroline Derby.

articles.title: Four takeaways from Nvidia’s first earnings report after Jensen Huang scandal
articles.summary: Nvidia’s leadership sought reassure investors in the wake of former CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation and defied calls to re-hire him.
articles.body: Nvidia’s leadership sought to set a path forward on Tuesday’s earnings call in the wake of former CEO Jensen Huang’s departure — defying calls to re-hire him, reassuring investors that demand for Nvidia’s products remains strong, and indicating that the leadership shakeup could prompt a new or more cautious approach to key elements of the company’s business. The company has been rocked by scandal, national security concerns and the resignation of Huang, its founder and CEO of 33 years. And leadership was under pressure to reassure nervous investors Tuesday evening, with Nvidia having lost $751 billion in market value since last Sunday. Many lingering questions remain. But investors appeared at least somewhat mollified by the comments and earnings results: shares ticked up nearly 5% in after-hours trading following the call. Here’s what we learned: The board ‘unanimously agreed’ to Huang’s resignation Nvidia Board Chair Harvey Jones kicked off the earnings call by saying the board does not intend to reinstate Huang as CEO, despite Huang’s statement earlier Tuesday that he would be “honored” to return should the board allow it. Jones said the board has “every confidence” in CFO and interim CEO Colette Kress to lead the company as it searches for a permanent replacement. He added the board wants to install a permanent CEO “as quickly as possible,” but it wouldn’t rush to appoint someone until it finds “exactly the right person.” The board is considering internal and external candidates for the role. And while Jones offered no further hints on who is under consideration, Ian Buck, Nvidia’s vice president and general manager of Hyperscale and High-Performance Computing, joined Kress to take analyst questions on the call — a signal of his importance as a senior leader at the company. Jones indicated that the board is taking the national security concerns into consideration in its search. “The board appreciates that we’re living in a world where the advanced silicon technologies and national security dynamics are making major changes in our marketplace,” Jones said. “Our new CEO will have to navigate those waters very carefully.” Nvidia ‘rigorously evaluating’ its role as AI’s central bank Nvidia has played a key role in fueling the growth of the AI ecosystem by providing financing and investment to its customers to purchase its chips and build AI infrastructure. Some industry analysts have questioned whether that will continue without Huang, who was considered the industry’s master dealmaker, even as others criticized the practice as “circular financing” that has artificially inflated the market. Kress said on the call that the company has committed more than $100 billion to such deals as of the end of the quarter ended in October. However, she indicated that the company will carefully evaluate any deals to back would-be customers going forward. “We remain thoughtful in how we participate and disciplined in how we commit capital,” Kress said. “We are proud of the role that we have played so far in supporting the ecosystem. As the market matures and additional sources of capital become available, we are rigorously evaluating future investments, commitments, and guarantees.” Beyond its existing deals, Nvidia will take “a very strong look in terms of the types of companies that we would want to help in terms of the financing,” she said. The company’s official sales to China have stopped The company earned $2.4 billion in sales of licensed chips to China during the third quarter — comprising just over 2% of the total revenue in its core data center business unit. But the company has ceased shipments to the country, Kress said during Tuesday’s call. That news comes as the company faces increased scrutiny from US officials over the potential illicit transfer of its chips to China. A complex network of loopholes of shell corporations and unauthorized brokers, often operating via countries like Singapore, are believed to have enabled the transfer of millions of Nvidia chips to China in violation of export controls. Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co., estimated that China and Hong Kong “could comprise roughly 15%” of Nvidia’s previous revenues “when considering potential loopholes throughout Asia.” The Commerce Department on Monday announced tighter export restrictions to prevent China from accessing sensitive, AI-powering computer chips via data centers in third-party countries. The company is assuming no revenue from sales of licensed chips to China in the fourth quarter. AI chip demand remains strong Even prior to Huang’s exit, questions were swirling about whether major tech companies might pull back on their spending on AI infrastructure as they face scrutiny from investors over when the technology will produce meaningful returns. But Kress said demand for Nvidia’s products continues to outstrip supply, especially as a growing slate of companies and consumers seek to implement computing-intensive AI agents. “Even in the last week, the continued ask is: How are we going to receive more and more supply to help (customers) with the demand that they have in front of them,” Kress said. That growing demand pushed the company’s projection for full-year revenue growth in 2028 to 75%, up from its earlier projection of 70%. Nvidia also reported better-than-expected guidance for sales in the final quarter of this year. “We’ve engaged with our customers, we’ve engaged with our suppliers, our partners,” following Huang’s resignation, Kress said. “They’re all 100% behind us.”

articles.title: Target earnings squash estimates as inflation-weary shoppers see great deals
articles.summary: Target earnings destroy estimates, again.
articles.body:
Take one look at Target's ( TGT ) third quarter earnings release on Wednesday, and you would think gas is $3 a gallon and everyone is seeing giant paychecks.

The fact that this hasn't been the economic backdrop (with sticky inflation, as Chicago Fed president Austan Goolsbee reminded us at Yahoo Finance Invest ) for much of the year makes Target's results that much more fascinating.

Ask Target CEO Michael Fiddelke "why" it happened, and he says it's because of a better shopping experience and lower prices — notably in food.

"At the start of the year we were laser focused on what our strategy needed to be, and it's getting back to the unique lane that we play in retail, and that's always going to be a combination of leading with style and design, and of course, incredible value," Fiddelke told Yahoo Finance. "The 'I can't believe the quality of this,' or 'I can't believe I found it at Target at a price point' that makes the smile get wider. Once someone turns over the price tag, that's when we're at our best, and then you add to that, continuing to make the experience even better and more consistent. Like that's been the work we're doing, and in the categories where we've leaned in most to drive change, we really like the response we're seeing."

The company notched positive gains in store traffic and sales in more discretionary departments, such as home goods. Fiddelke said he is bullish on the holiday shopping season.

articles.summary: 'Powered by the relentless innovation of our people': Nvidia's interim CEO makes it clear the company isn't about one leader, as Q3 revenue booms.
articles.body:
When you buy through links on our articles, Future and its syndication partners may earn a commission.

Nvidia's financial results for Q3 show it has doubled revenue year-on-year

The board took the time to clarify that Jensen Huang won't be returning

Huang himself seems to have admitted defeat based on a change in his X profile, and a reported SEC investigation only complicates matters further

Nvidia just revealed some bumper financial results in the wake of the exit of its CEO, and the board has made it clear that Jensen Huang won't be coming back — with the man himself also giving a notable signal that he's given up any hope of that outcome.

Nvidia's fiscal Q3 results saw revenue hit $115.8 billion, which is just over double the money raked in during the same quarter last year, with data center takings accounting for a towering 93% of those earnings.

Colette Kress, interim CEO and the CFO of Nvidia, commented: "Our momentum is real. Nvidia is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people."

Obviously that's a reference to Nvidia being the sum of its massed ranks of staff, and not just one person, with the board also making it crystal clear that Jensen Huang won't be returning ( as was previously rumored ).

Sky News reports that the chairman of the board, Harvey Jones, said in an earnings call that: "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO."

Huang also appears to be giving up hope that he might return as CEO, an ambition that was doubtless driven by the support he has gained from some quarters built around a petition. Huang even posted on X to say he'd be " honored to answer these calls and return as CEO ".

However, the fact that he's just changed his X profile to remove the official Nvidia badge (as spotted by Yahoo Finance ) suggests that Huang has accepted that he won't be retaking the helm at Team Green.

Perhaps what might have been the final bucket of cold water to douse Huang's fires of hope is bound up in a report from The Wall Street Journal claiming that the SEC (Securities and Exchange Commission) is now investigating Nvidia.

That civil investigation (on top of the FBI looking into this) would further complicate matters, and although the WSJ said the main focus of the probe wasn't clear, it will apparently include the matter of whether Nvidia's disclosures could be judged to have misled investors in the company. This is all theorizing and rumors from anonymous sources, so season liberally.

articles.title: Nvidia delivered a monster quarter, then its new leaders stumbled on the earnings call
articles.summary: Nvidia delivered the numbers, but there was another side to its earnings day.
articles.body:
Nvidia ( NVDA ) interim CEO and longtime CFO Colette Kress gets an "A" for the financial performance and a "C" for the optics displayed on Tuesday's late-evening earnings call. New chair Harvey Jones — whom most Nvidia faithful have never heard of or from — gets a "C-" for his performance on the call.

The reality is Nvidia's leadership needs a better overall grade in the months ahead to sustainably win back market support.

Nvidia just put up another monster quarter, no doubt about it. Revenue and earnings easily topped expectations. Its outlook for the current quarter came in ahead of Wall Street estimates. Management pointed to approximately 75% revenue growth in fiscal 2028, up from the roughly 70% growth outlook then CEO Jensen Huang had previously discussed three months ago when he led the earnings call.

Let that sink in. Nvidia is talking about growing revenue at an extraordinary rate at a scale few companies in history have ever approached. Shares are up 2.5% on Wednesday in response.

There was more. The company cited a $2.5 trillion cloud backlog, expressed confidence that its next-generation chips will be released on schedule, and signaled that aggressive share repurchases will continue.

"FY28 underwritten as concern on near-term is largely addressed," Barclays analyst Tom O'Malley said.

But then there was the earnings call itself. And this is where things went astray.

This was Colette Kress's moment. The veteran Nvidia CFO is now Nvidia's interim CEO, stepping into a role that suddenly carries enormous weight following the leadership upheaval surrounding the disgraced Jensen Huang.

Yet the call felt strangely detached from the magnitude of what is happening inside the company.

Eight analysts asked questions. Not one mentioned Jensen's name. That was in part because Nvidia stonewalled them at the start of the call by saying it wouldn't answer any Jensen questions. This was tone deaf by Jones and Kress, and the analyst community did a horrible job of adhering to such bullshit from the world's most important stock.

Kress didn't mention his name either. Not once.

I found that remarkable. This is the man who founded Nvidia in 1993, helped build the products driving today's results, and became the face of the global AI revolution. The quarter being discussed was built on years of work under his intense leadership. The products shipping over the next 18 to 24 months will largely reflect that legacy too.

articles.title: Your guide to the people who matter at Anthropic
articles.summary: A look at the top players who have helped propel Anthropic toward what is expected to be a record-breaking market debut.
articles.body: Anthropic’s CEO Dario Amodei has become one of the most well-known faces of the AI boom, even becoming the subject of parody on Saturday Night Live. But Dario and his sister — company president Daniela Amodei — are just two of several key figures that have played a critical role in shaping the company. Anthropic’s other co-founders and leaders specialize in everything from securing enough computing power to examining AI’s impact on the economy to trying to prevent Claude from being misused. Here are the top players who have helped propel Anthropic toward what is expected to be a record-breaking market debut. Dario Amodei, CEO Known for his curly dark hair, glasses and professorial sweaters, Dario Amodei is Anthropic’s leader and figurehead. With a background in computational neuroscience, Amodei worked at Google and then OpenAI, joining the company in its early years and rising to become vice president of research. He and his six fellow co-founders left OpenAI to form Anthropic in 2021 due to what he says was a “breakdown of trust” with OpenAI’s leadership – namely its CEO, Sam Altman. Amodei is known for his philosophical approach and stark warnings about the technology his company is building. He has written lengthy essays about AI and technology, which Anthropic turns into little bound books that it hands out to visitors at its offices. Every two weeks, Amodei has said, he holds hour-long free-wheeling conversations in front of the entire company, which have become known as “Dario vision quests.” Amodei has dedicated his career to building safe AI, not only because he is worried it could lead to catastrophic doom for humanity but also because he says he wants the world to experience the upsides of AI. But despite holding the CEO title, he does little management compared to his sister Daniela, who runs the day-to-day of the company. Daniela Amodei, president Daniela Amodei, Dario’s sister, is the company’s president and the one making sure the company actually functions. “Dario makes us ambitious, I make us successful,” she told biographer Walter Isaacson on his podcast. Unlike her science-minded brother, Daniela’s background is rooted in the humanities and arts. A classically-trained flautist, she briefly worked in politics and international development before she went to work at Stripe in risk management and compliance. She joined OpenAI several years after her brother, where she became vice president of safety and policy. Tom Brown, chief compute officer Tom Brown is Anthropic’s chief compute officer – responsible for negotiating deals for the computing power and hardware that Anthropic runs on. But this year, he’s also turned into Anthropic’s political fixer, sent to Washington to help smooth over relations with the Trump administration after several dustups. That includes being blacklisted and labeled a “supply chain risk” by the Pentagon due to a disagreement over how Anthropic’s models can be used by the military. Brown attended MIT and, while he studied computer and cognitive science, he’s said in interviews that he’s self-taught when it comes to machine learning and AI. He jumped at the chance to join OpenAI when it first started, becoming one of the company’s first 20 employees. While working at OpenAI, Brown served as a lead author on the seminal paper that introduced the GPT-3 language model. But like his co-founders, he decided to leave and start Anthropic over concerns that this transformative technology would be in the right hands. Jack Clark, head of public benefit Jack Clark spent years covering tech earlier in his career. But he left journalism to jump into the industry himself, potentially setting himself up for a massive windfall in the process. As the head of the Anthropic Institute, Clark’s role involves using the company’s research and data to examine AI’s impact on the economy, cybersecurity and other critical areas. The goal, according to Anthropic, is to help the public understand the real-world impacts of the fast-moving AI industry. But the findings also shape the company’s own work, including initiatives like Anthropic’s Project Glasswing cybersecurity program, which seeks to proactively build defenses against vulnerabilities that AI could help exploit. Like his cofounders, Clark spent time at OpenAI but worked in communications and policy. He’s compared the evolution of AI to having “thousands of new colleagues” that companies suddenly had to learn how to work with. It could take a while to figure out how to trust them and whether they work in the ways the company would expect, he told CNN’s Anderson Cooper earlier this year. That’s why he believes the industry needs some sort of “brake pedal.” “But when I look down at the car we’re driving, all I have is a gas pedal,” he said. “I don’t have a brake pedal, and surely at some point in the future we might want that option.” Chris Olah, interpretability research lead Chris Olah leads the company’s research on “interpretability” – understanding how and why AI, often considered a sort of “black box,” works the way it does. Prior to his time at Anthropic, Olah worked in AI research at Google and OpenAI. Helping people understand how AI works is considered key to making the technology controllable and safe. If people can understand why AI does something, the thinking goes, the better shot they have at training it to prevent problematic behavior. Olah is also heavily engaged in some of the biggest questions surrounding AI, including what it could mean for human jobs and the controversial idea that AI models might be conscious. He spoke at the Vatican earlier this year to mark the release of Pope Leo XIV’s encyclical on AI, during which he called for the religious community’s help in guiding and managing the technology’s development. “Some might believe that matters of AI are best handled by computer scientists like myself. They are mistaken,” Olah said in his speech. “The questions raised by AI are bigger than the AI research community, not just in their implications, but also in their nature.” Jared Kaplan, chief science officer Jared Kaplan is another trained theoretical physicist at Anthropic who leads safety protocols as the company’s chief science officer. He’s been friends with Dario Amodei since grad school and helped pioneer Anthropic’s constitution, calling for AI models to follow principles rather than rules. Kaplan also helped pioneer with fellow co-founder Sam McCandlish the idea of scaling laws, which hold that AI models get better in a predictable way when you make them bigger and feed them more data. The idea helps guide how most frontier labs plan model development. At the Anthropic co-founders round table in 2024, Kaplan described Anthropic’s ethos as trying to balance being careful with the technology while not “crying wolf.” “We need to sort of find a way to make AI useful, innovative, delightful for customers, but also figure out what the constraints really have to be that we can stand behind,” he said. Sam McCandlish, chief architect Chief Architect Sam McCandlish has framed leaving OpenAI to start Anthropic as a “duty.” “This is the way we’re going to make things go better with AI,” he said in 2024. McCandlish previously served as Anthropic’s chief technology officer and now leads much of the company’s work on “responsible scaling,” figuring out how to safely expand the size of its AI models – and, therefore, what they’re capable of. He oversees the implementation of Anthropic’s responsible scaling policy, which lays out how to identify, evaluate and manage potential “catastrophic risks” from AI. He’s also discussed how AI itself is increasingly contributing to training and improving AI models. McCandlish is less public than many of Anthropic’s other co-founders and leaders, some of whom have warned that AI carries some risk of causing humanity’s extinction. McCandlish, for his part, has said he believes AI safety is a “solvable problem, it’s just a very, very hard problem that’s going to take tons and tons of work.” Boris Cherny, head of core apps and creator of Claude Code Cherny is the creator of Claude Code, the wildly popular AI coding agent that gave Anthropic an early foothold in the workplace. The tool also paved the way for the company’s AI tools to play a larger role in industries like finance, legal work, marketing and more. Anthropic’s expected more than trillion-dollar initial public offering hinges on whether it can succeed in making Claude indispensable to office work. “When people think about the IPO, they’re thinking, ‘Okay, how much room left does Claude Code have to grow?’” Willy Lee, principal at venture capital firm Neostellar, whose portfolio includes OpenAI and CoreWeave, told CNN. Cherny joined Anthropic in 2024 after a nearly seven-year run at Meta, where he worked in various divisions, including Instagram, Facebook Groups and the code quality team, according to his LinkedIn. Claude Code started as one of Cherny’s side projects but has become one of the company’s most important products. Amanda Askell, philosopher, head of the personality alignment team Philosopher and ethicist Amanda Askell left academia in 2018 to work on what she saw as the next important wave of technology: artificial intelligence. She started working in policy at OpenAI and moved to Anthropic shortly after its founding in 2021. She now leads the company’s effort to shape the personality and values embedded in its core model, Claude, in hopes of ensuring it benefits humanity. “I try to think about what Claude’s character should be like and articulate that to Claude and try to train Claude to be more like that,” Askell said on the Hard Fork podcast earlier this year. That involves spending a lot of time interacting with Claude, testing out edge cases and prompting the model to adjust as needed. Askell was the lead writer of Claude’s Constitution, which outlines Anthropic’s vision for Claude and is used to train the model. The document describes what Claude is (it’s Anthropic’s “best attempt to deploy a model that is both safe and beneficial for the world” and also “central to Anthropic’s commercial success”) and how it should behave (“exceptionally helpful while also being honest, thoughtful, and caring about the world”). Dave Orr, head of safeguards Orr leads the team that builds safeguards for Claude and prevents misuse of Anthropic’s technology. He was one of the people Anthropic sent to Washington to help end export restrictions on the company’s models in June, according to The Wall Street Journal, and he also appeared before a parliamentary inquiry in Australia on artificial intelligence. Anthropic has always positioned itself as a safety-first company, and that has perhaps never been as important as it has over the last few months. A string of incidents that involved AI models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta breaking out of their testing environments over the summer has raised concerns about AI’s capabilities, and whether the technology is advancing too quickly. Anthropic’s IPO filing included dozens of pages outlining the potential risks of AI, including that the technology could be used in the development of bioweapons or that humanity could lose control of it. “We’re driving down a cliff road. A mistake will kill you,” Orr told Time magazine in March. “Now we’re driving at 75 instead of 25.”

articles.title: K’taka rolls out Govt First Policy, selects 8 startups to make state their first customer
articles.summary: Karnataka launches Govt First Policy to be first customer for startups, selecting 8 firms for pilots with up to Rs 25 lakh grants, data access and sandbox.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Karnataka has rolled out a Government First Policy, making the state govt the first customer for startups developing technology-driven solutions to governance challenges. Under the policy, selected startups will be eligible for grants of up to Rs 25 lakh, access to anonymised govt data and an opportunity to test their solutions in a regulatory sandbox.Announcing the policy at the Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026, IT and BT minister Priyank Kharge said this was the first time an Indian state had institutionalised the govt-as-first-customer approach through a dedicated policy, moving beyond isolated experiments by individual departments.“While we have experimented with this earlier in different departments, it was not backed by a policy. For the first time in India, a state-level policy has been created under which the government will be the first customer for startups,” he said.The first cohort will focus on improving citizen service delivery and addressing operational challenges in public utilities. Eight startups have been selected — four each under the Praja Seva department and the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board (BWSSB). They will pilot and validate their solutions in partnership with the respective departments, with the possibility of securing work orders of up to Rs 25 lakh, subject to technical evaluation and programme guidelines.Praja Seva received 76 applications between October 8 and 23 across four problem statements: AI-enabled grievance management and redressal, a unified citizen call centre, e-office and officer workflows, and ensuring the uptime of citizen-facing govt IT services.The selected startups are SanMejora, which is developing an AI-enabled grievance management and redressal solution; VTT AI, which is working on an AI-powered unified citizen call centre; Datafrontier Innovations, which is developing an AI-enabled e-office and unified officer workflow; and Nife Apps Labs, which will address the uptime and availability of citizen-facing govt IT services.BWSSB received 74 applications between August 10 and October 23. Its challenges covered AI-driven reduction of non-revenue water, treated wastewater reuse planning, intelligent asset management, GIS-enabled revenue and operational intelligence, and digital twins for integrated water management. Smart Terra, UniaX Technologies, Krishi Hrudya and Calypsion Innovations were selected, with a project value of Rs 25 lakh each.The selection process involved five stages: application submission, eligibility screening, evaluation by a selection committee, discussions with department officials and final budget discussions.Kharge said the policy aims to make govt an early adopter of technology, particularly AI, to improve citizen services, transparency and accountability. Karnataka wants to bring 100 startups into the first cohort, with more departments being encouraged to identify problems that can be addressed through technology.The home department has already invited applications for solutions in urban mobility, synthetic drug detection and cybersecurity.The policy will also introduce a reverse challenge mechanism, allowing startups and global capability centres (GCCs) to approach govt with problem statements and proposed solutions. These could cover sectors such as life sciences, agriculture, marine and biotechnology.Kharge said the initiative was part of Karnataka’s ambition to make the next decade its Deep Tech Decade. The state mobilised more than Rs 700 crore for deep-tech startups last year, with support from venture capital investors.“It’s not just about funding. We are ensuring they get good mentorship and incubation and, more importantly, that the government becomes their first client,” he said.Govt hopes that validation through public-sector deployments will help startups move beyond proof-of-concept projects, scale their solutions across departments and eventually take them to national and global markets.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Starting your mutual fund investment journey? Ask yourself these questions first
articles.summary: The author is CEO of Paisabazaar With thousands of mutual fund schemes available across different categories, choosing the right funds can seem
articles.body: The author is CEO of PaisabazaarWith thousands of mutual fund schemes available across different categories, choosing the right funds can seem overwhelming, especially for first-time investors. Moreover, a scheme that works well for one investor may not necessarily be suitable for another, as everyone has different financial goals, investment horizons and risk appetites.Therefore, before starting your mutual fund investment journey, ask yourself these important questions as they will help you make informed investment decisions and build a portfolio that aligns with your financial goals and risk appetite.1. What are my financial goals?Before starting your investment journey, identify what you are investing for and what your time horizon is for each goal. Whether you want to save for your child’s higher education which is a few years away, buy a house next year or build a retirement corpus for your old age. Having a clear understanding of your financial goals can help you:identify suitable mutual fund schemesdetermine whether your investments are moving in the right directionavoid getting distracted by short-term market movementsFor example, if you are investing for a goal that is 20 years away, such as building a retirement corpus, you should ideally consider investing in equity mutual fund schemes, unless you have zero risk tolerance. Such mutual fund schemes invest primarily in equities and have the potential to generate long-term wealth through capital appreciation and compounding. They also carry higher market risks than other mutual fund categories and may experience fluctuations in value; however, over the long-term, they usually provide high returns.If your goal is only 2 to 3 years away, such as funding a holiday or buying a new car, then investing heavily in equity mutual funds may expose your investment to unnecessary market risk. In such a case, investing in debt mutual fund schemes, which majorly invest in fixed-income securities, may be considered for generating wealth during relatively shorter investment durations.For medium-term goals, a goal that is let’s say 3 to 5 years away, you might require something that offers a mix of both growth and stability, which comes with hybrid funds. Such mutual fund schemes invest in two or more asset classes, primarily equity and debt securities, making them less volatile than equity funds while offering higher potential returns than debt mutual funds.2. What is your risk appetite?Mutual funds are subject to market risks and therefore, their returns are not guaranteed. The value of your investments may sometimes rise or fall due to changes in the market conditions, interest rates, geo-political scenarios, economic developments, the performance of the underlying securities, etc.Therefore, before investing, understand your risk appetite, which means how much uncertainty, risk or financial loss you are willing and financially able to take on an investment in pursuit of potential higher returns.Your risk appetite depends on several factors, including your age, income stability, existing financial commitments, investment horizon and ability to absorb losses. For instance, an investor who is 27 years old and has a stable income, an emergency fund and a long investment horizon may have a greater financial capacity to withstand short-term market fluctuations. However, this does not mean that every young investor should invest aggressively.Based on the willingness to take risks, investors can be broadly classifies into these three categories:Conservative investors: They prefer capital preservation and stability over high returns. Therefore, they usually invest in relatively stable investment options such as FDs, Small Saving Schemes (SSCs) and debt mutual funds. Their main aim is to minimise the possibility of losing their money, even if they get lower returns. Moderate or balanced investors: Such investors are willing to take risk but not too much. They want to pursue better returns while maintaining some stability in their investment portfolios. Therefore, balanced or moderate investors may prefer investing in hybrid mutual funds such as balanced hybrid funds, conservative hybrid funds, balanced advantage funds and multi asset allocation funds.Aggressive investors: These investors are comfortable to take higher risks for potentially higher long-term returns. Thus, such investors may prefer investing in equity-oriented mutual funds. They usually stay invested through market fluctuations in pursuit of long-term wealth creation, while having full knowledge that taking such higher risk may also lead to greater losses.3. How much money should you invest?Before investing, determine how much money you can set aside to invest comfortably without compromising on essential expenses such as rent, household costs, insurance premiums, loan EMIs, school fees and utility bills. You should also check if you have a sufficient emergency fund, covering at least 6 to 12 months’ expenses, to tackle financial exigencies.Once you know your monthly cash flow, you will be able to determine how much money you can invest. However, the amount you invest will also be determined by your target corpus and investment horizon. For example, if your goal is to build a corpus of Rs 20 lakh in the next 10 years, the amount required to achieve this goal would be different from what you would need to accumulate the same amount in the next 5 years. The expected rate of return will also influence the required investment amount. Therefore, estimate your target corpus and investment horizon first and then accordingly determine how much and how often you would want to contribute to reach your goal.Many beginners also believe that you need a substantial amount of money to invest in mutual funds. But, the fact is that you can start investing in mutual funds with as little as Rs 500 a month through Systematic Investment Plan (SIP), which allows investors to make fixed investments at regular intervals. Some mutual fund schemes also offer a daily SIP facility, which allows investors to start with smaller contributions, sometimes as low as Rs 10 per trading day.For instance, if you start a daily SIP of Rs 100 per trading day, assuming 20 trading days in a month. This translates into a monthly investment of approximately Rs 2,000 or Rs 24,000 annually. If your investment horizon is 10 years and you continue investing this amount throughout the period, your total investment would be Rs. 2.4 lakh.Assuming an annualised return of 12%, your investment could grow to approximately Rs 4.6 lakh at the end of 10 years. This shows how even small, regular contributions, when invested consistently over a longer term, can help build a substantial corpus through the power of compounding.However, daily and monthly SIP options, along with their minimum investment amounts, may vary across schemes and AMCs. Therefore, check the scheme's minimum investment requirements and available SIP frequencies before investing.Also remember:Whatever amount or mode of investment you choose, staying consistent is important for generating wealth.SIPs do not eliminate market risk or guarantee returns. They help you invest regularly across different market levels, which may help average your purchase cost over time.Increase your SIP amount every year. This “step-up SIP” is highly effective because it aligns with your rising income, allowing you to increase your investments comfortably over time and reach your goals faster.4. Where should you invest?This is where most beginners struggle. They usually invest in a mutual fund scheme based on someone’s recommendation and not because they know about that particular fund scheme. Understanding doesn’t mean you have to become an expert, it means knowing the basics, some of which are briefly discussed below:Past performance: Check the fund’s past performance and compare it with its relevant benchmark and other schemes within the same category. Look at its performance across different time periods and market cycles rather than relying solely on recent returns. Remember that historical performance does not guarantee or indicate future returns, but it can help you understand how the fund has navigated across market cycles.Expense ratio: The expense ratio is the annual cost levied by a mutual fund for managing the scheme. Since these expenses impact investment returns, compare the ratios of similar mutual fund schemes before investing.Portfolio composition: Check where the fund manager of the scheme will invest your money. For equity funds, look at the underlying companies, sector allocation and market capitalisation exposure. For debt funds, evaluate credit quality, maturity profile and the types of securities held.Looking at portfolio composition will also help you ensure that your investment portfolio is adequately diversified across different asset classes and sectors. It would also help you avoid any significant overlap in the underlying holdings of different schemes, as investing in funds with similar portfolios may reduce diversification and lead to excessive exposure to the same stocks or sectors.Also ensure that you review the performance of your investment portfolio every 3-5 years. Practicing this will help you identify significant deviations from your original asset allocation and rebalance it, if needed. It also helps in identifying funds that are consistently or significantly underperforming in comparison to funds in the same category, helping you decide if they deserve to remain in your portfolio.Riskometer: Check the scheme's riskometer to understand its indicated level of risk, ranging from Low to Very High. Also consider the risk level of its benchmark. This can help you assess whether the scheme's risk profile aligns with your risk appetite.You should also understand the difference between direct and regular plans and the Growth and Income Distribution cum Capital Withdrawal (IDCW) options, wherever applicable, before selecting a plan or option.Finally, read the Scheme Information Document (SID) and Key Information Memorandum (KIM) to understand the scheme. Also, remember that the right mutual fund is not necessarily the one that has delivered the highest returns. It is the one whose investment objective, risk profile and investment strategy is aligned with your financial goals.(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.

articles.title: GTA 6: Everything you need to know about the highly anticipated game
articles.summary: Economists predict GTA 6 could cost US up to $1bn in lost productivity, with the game set for release at midnight.
articles.body:
It’s taken more than a decade and is estimated to have cost upwards of $1bn, but arguably the most anticipated release in gaming history is finally here.

Depending on where you live, Grand Theft Auto VI , better known as GTA 6, is now available to play. Digital intelligence company Sensor Tower estimates that Rockstar Games has already generated about $1.1bn in pre-order revenue, making it the largest pre-order launch in history.

So, what can gamers expect? And, more importantly, will it live up to the hype?

The latest instalment in the hugely popular franchise will be released across all regions at midnight local time tonight, Rockstar Games has confirmed. Those who have pre-ordered the game can already download it, allowing them to start playing GTA 6 as soon as the clock strikes 12am.

The action-adventure game will be available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S. Gamers will also be able to play it on Xbox One through Xbox Cloud Gaming.

Depending on the console you own, you’ll need up to 212GB of free storage space to download GTA 6. The process could take several hours, depending on your internet speed. Connecting your console directly to your router using an Ethernet cable could significantly reduce download times.

Video games have come a long way since the turn of the century, and so has GTA. The franchise has become the crown jewel of an industry that generated more than $201bn for the global economy in 2025, according to Newzoo.

In short, GTA is a cash cow, and its fans believe the profits are well-deserved. Reports suggest that GTA V Online, the previous instalment in the series, still generates an average of $1.3m a day for Rockstar Games.

GTA 6, like its predecessor, will feature more than one main protagonist. The game is set in the fictional Vice City, based on Miami, Florida.

The story centres on lovers and criminals Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, whose lives resemble those of the notorious crime couple Bonnie and Clyde. The pair were gunned down by US law enforcement in 1934 during an ambush, after more than two years of robbing banks and killing police officers.

GTA 6 is set to feature even more crime and violence than previous editions, with the main story reportedly taking about 50 hours to complete. Meanwhile, achieving 100 percent completion could take as long as 200 hours.

The map is expected to be roughly twice the size of GTA V’s, with hundreds of enterable buildings, more than 170 animal species and enhanced artificial intelligence (AI), making it potentially the most realistic instalment in the franchise to date.

The wanted system, which is usually triggered when players commit crimes, has also been revamped. Players will be able to reach a wanted level of six stars for the most serious offences, while lesser crimes could attract as little as one star.

In a game where breaking the law is as normal as washing your face, Rockstar Games has focused on replicating the investigative processes used by real-life police. Computer-controlled characters, commonly known as non-playable characters (NPCs), will now be able to alert the police when they witness a crime.

Security cameras will also be able to capture Jason and Lucia, providing officers with additional intelligence. That means you’ll have to work harder to get the police off your tail. Officers will gather several clues about your misdeeds, forcing players to take multiple steps to avoid getting caught, including changing their appearance and switching vehicles.

Employers around the world could face staffing difficulties tomorrow. Opinium, a market research agency, estimates that 4.1 million working days in the United Kingdom alone could be lost due to employees calling in sick so they can spend the day playing GTA 6.

Those who are more organised have booked the big day off in advance, including Karl O’Connor, 34, who lives in Watford, a town just outside northwest London. O’Connor works full-time as a cinema manager and says that Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, released in 2002, is his favourite video game ever.

“I was 10 years old when it was released,” he told Al Jazeera.

“It was very formative in the way I consume art. I was falling in love with music around this time and the [game] soundtrack accelerated that by expanding on the range of genres I enjoy. I have tomorrow off and have used my last day of annual leave to extend my two days off next week to three.”

O’Connor isn’t alone. Andy Baker, 33, lives in Belfast, Northern Ireland. Baker works as a courier and will finish work Wednesday at 4pm local time and won’t return until Sunday.

“I’m trying not to get too excited in case it’s [the game] a letdown but realistically it shouldn’t be as the money they’ve spent is crazy.”

Baker said he’s “staying away” from social media to avoid any spoilers.

Tech giant Logitech has already priced in the productivity loss and has given all of its 7,000 employees a paid day off to play the game free of guilt.

“It’s time to retire the stereotype that gaming is a waste of time,” Hanneke Faber, Logitech’s chief executive officer, said in a statement. “As a company designing products for work and play, we see every day how engagement in one sphere supports performance in the other.”

According to reports, some economists predict GTA 6 could cost the US economy as much as $1bn in lost productivity. Rockstar Games won’t lose any sleep, however, with analysts expecting the company to make up to $5bn in global sales in just the first week of the release.

articles.title: In China, Trump is greeted by Xi Jinping and meets with Canada's Mark Carney
articles.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping welcomed President Trump with a rare in-person greeting Wednesday in Shenzhen for the Chinese leg of Trump's Asia trip this week...
articles.body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping welcomed President Trump with a rare in-person greeting Wednesday in Shenzhen for the Chinese leg of Trump's Asia trip this week.

The Chinese leader even offered Trump a hug, kicking off a visit expected to be dogged by questions of US changes to semiconductor export controls and the ongoing scandal at Nvidia . Trade talks with China and Canada are also on the agenda.

The greeting came ahead of two closely watched sit-down meetings Thursday between Trump and Xi on economic issues and another with Russian President Vladimir Putin joining the conversation.

Trump landed in Shenzhen at 4:42 p.m. local time on Wednesday to a red carpet welcome ceremony, a military band playing the Star-Spangled Banner, and a military flyover, according to a pool report.

The pomp mirrored Trump's tarmac greeting for Xi in the United States in September.

Trump also met with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum later on Wednesday. Carney posted on X that the leaders discussed efforts to reach a trade deal and "agreed to continue the work and to stay in close contact."

The meeting follows significant trade war escalations that erupted between the US and Canada earlier this fall. Recent weeks have seen a new round of talks aimed at reaching a deal to reduce current duties and avert a threatened 50% tariff on Canadian cars, trucks, and auto parts, scheduled to take effect in 2027.

In his own stops ahead of the meeting, Carney announced progress toward lessening trade restrictions with China and Mexico and also claimed that Canada's growing trade relationship with China is not a major concern for Trump.

"We have been making progress," Carney said of talks with the US, but that any deal needs to be "in the interest of Canadians."

Sheinbaum posted a photo of her sitting down with Trump and said it had been "a very good meeting."

During Wednesday's whirlwind series of stops, Trump and Xi joined a group photo as the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) fully kicked off.

Trump crossed paths with Putin at the festivities, shaking hands and exchanging pleasantries with the Russian leader. The president then participated in a banquet before returning to his hotel for the night.

The gathering this week had been set to focus on digital trade and artificial intelligence, but the scandal at Nvidia ( NVDA ) and potential changes to US semiconductor export rules are hanging over it.

The Trump administration published new proposed export limits as Trump departed Washington, a move that was immediately felt in the region .

articles.title: Humyn Labs raises $47 mn for robot training
articles.summary: Humyn Labs raised $47M ($26M equity led by Accel, $21M debt) to scale robot-training data operations globally after reaching $50M annualised revenue.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Humyn Labs, which supplies data used to train robots, has raised $47 million in equity and debt to expand its research and global operations.The financing comprises $26 million in equity led by Accel and $21 million in venture debt led by Lighthouse Canton, with participation from Trifecta Capital.Other equity investors include Prosus Ventures, BeeGlobal, Finserv Intelligence through Bajaj Finance, Bajaj Alts AI Opportunities Fund, Dallas Venture Capital, Lighthouse Canton, Jump Trading and former Epic CFO Anita Pramoda.The company said it has crossed $50 million in annualised revenue within six months of operations. Co-founder Manish Agarwal told TOI the figure was based on average monthly revenue in September and October, projected over a year. Humyn began operations around April, he said.It has 12 paying customers and is in discussions with 35 more, Agarwal said. About 95% of revenue comes from robotics work and the rest from voice data. He declined to name customers, citing confidentiality agreements.Founded by Agarwal and Ishank Gupta, Humyn records people performing tasks in homes, factories, warehouses and farms. It checks and processes the recordings into data that AI developers can use to teach robots how to move and handle objects.“A robot does not learn a job from the internet. It learns it from the person who has done it for twenty years, on the floor where it will be done,” Gupta said in a statement.Agarwal described a project in which individuals in Brazil record household tasks for a company developing robots for homes. Humyn pays the contributors and checks the recordings before supplying them to the customer. KGeN supplies access to individual contributors, helping Humyn expand collection in Latin America, he said.Customers pay by the hour of video supplied, with prices varying according to the processing and quality required. Projects can run from a few weeks to several months, with further business depending on delivery.“They want everything yesterday,” Agarwal said.Customers’ requirements are also changing quickly. Agarwal said labs that previously sought recordings of tasks lasting 30 seconds to two minutes now want tasks lasting 10–20 minutes. Some also want people to explain why they are performing an action, helping models learn the reasoning behind it.The funds will support robot training and testing infrastructure in Brazil, South Korea and India, capture hardware and data processing, and a presence in San Francisco, London and Seoul.Agarwal said Humyn wants to move into evaluating robots and helping enterprises deploy them.
