articles.title: Bill Gurley says giving away AI is Google's 'No. 1' move against Anthropic
articles.summary: Anthropic is winning on price as DeepSeek and other free Chinese models win AI's traffic.
articles.body:
Bill Gurley , the venture capitalist behind an early bet on Uber ( UBER ), has an idea for how Google could slow Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) down: Give the AI away.

Gurley, a general partner at Benchmark, told Deirdre Bosa Live on Monday that Alphabet's ( GOOGL ) Google should use free AI to keep Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) and OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ) from pulling away. Anthropic prices its IPO Wednesday and begins trading Thursday under the ticker symbol ANT .

"If Google recognizes that Anthropic ... and OpenAI maybe are getting escape velocity away from them, it is the No. 1 thing they should go do ... bar none," he said.

Gurley calls it playing defense. Open-weight models, which anyone can download, run and change for free, keep one company from locking up a market. Google did it with Kubernetes "when they were worried about Amazon and AWS," he said, and with Android "when they were worried about Apple having a monopoly in phones."

The catch? "We're not seeing those actions from Google."

Free models already do most of the work. On OpenRouter, a marketplace developers use to reach hundreds of AI models, seven of the 10 most-used models last week came from Chinese labs and are free to download. DeepSeek's V4.1 Flash alone processed about 77 trillion tokens, the basic units of text that AI models read and write. That's more than the other nine combined.

Duolingo ( DUOL ) CEO Luis von Ahn told Yahoo Finance last week that open models cut the cost of each AI video call to less than a cent from about 30 cents. "The vast majority of our usage of AI will be in open-weight models pretty soon," he said.

The money flows the other way. Closed models handled 28% of OpenRouter's tokens in mid-September but collected 73% of the spending, according to its September report . Similarly, Apple's ( AAPL ) iPhone accounted for about a fifth of phones sold in the second quarter but generated nearly half of revenue, according to Counterpoint Research.

Price is a big reason. Anthropic lists Claude Opus 5.5, its most-used model, at about 27 times what DeepSeek charges for its own. And while 39 companies sell DeepSeek's model on OpenRouter, nobody sells Claude Opus for less than Anthropic does. As Gurley put it, "The marginal price is going to equal marginal cost."

Gurley also called Anthropic's choice to write off model training costs right away, rather than over years, "pretty amazing," adding, "it's still profitable, really high gross margin."

articles.title: Wife of senior Nvidia executive embroiled in chip smuggling scandal
articles.summary: The wife of one of Jensen Huang’s most senior allies has been caught up in a chip-smuggling scandal that has engulfed one of Nvidia’s biggest partners.
articles.body:
The wife of one of Jensen Huang's most senior allies has been caught up in a chip-smuggling scandal that has engulfed one of Nvidia's biggest partners.

Cenly Chen, who is reportedly married to Jay Puri, an Nvidia executive, worked at Super Micro, a technology company where senior executives have been accused of smuggling $2.5bn (£1.9bn) worth of chips to China.

In a lawsuit brought by shareholders of Super Micro, investors allege there was "no way Cenly Chen lacked knowledge about the company's illicit sales". Super Micro has yet to file a response to the claims.

Ms Chen was previously chief growth officer at Super Micro, which packages Nvidia chips into computer servers.

US prosecutors charged some of the company's leading executives earlier this year over involvement in an illicit chip smuggling scheme.

Super Micro has insisted it has co-operated with the US government's investigation and has not been named in its indictment. Ms Chen is not named in the US charges.

However, the revelations come amid mounting scrutiny on Nvidia's ties to the Far East over claims Mr Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

Muddy waters, a short-selling firm, raised questions over Ms Chen's ties to Nvidia on Tuesday night.

The firm noted how Ms Chen had been repeatedly photographed alongside Mr Puri and named in photographs as Cenly Puri.

The pair are reportedly married, technology news site The Information reported on Wednesday.

Nvidia has already been the subject of intense pressure over claims that Chinese companies sought to access its chips through illegal smuggling and legal loopholes.

Nvidia's graphics chips are widely used to develop powerful AI technology.

The Super Micro scandal, which emerged earlier this year, saw Wally Liaw, the company's co-founder, charged by the US government for allegedly diverting advanced Nvidia chips via Taiwan to customers in China.

Mr Liaw has pleaded not guilty to the charges.

Mr Huang resigned last Thursday over claims he had a relationship with Alice Huang, who worked at another Nvidia customer, Megaspeed.

Megaspeed, based in Singapore, has also been investigated by the US for smuggling over claims it diverted powerful Nvidia chips to China. The company has denied wrongdoing.

Nvidia's board rejected an attempt by Mr Huang to return to the company on Tuesday, insisting it had no plans to reinstate him.

The fallout has also triggered scrutiny in the White House.

It emerged on Wednesday that leading Democrats in the US House of Representatives have launched an investigation into whether Howard Lutnick, the US commerce secretary, had used his position to help Cantor Fitzgerald avoid losses from the Nvidia scandal.

articles.title: B’luru ranks second in Asia among AI startup clusters; K’taka ecosystem valued at $153bn: Report
articles.summary: Bengaluru ranks 2nd in Asia for AI startups; Karnataka startup ecosystem valued at $153bn, drew $39bn VC (2021-25) and raised $1.5bn for AI since 2020.
articles.body: Bengaluru: From avarekai (hyacinth beans) to AI, masala dose to machine learning, and filter coffee to frontier models, that’s how Siddarth Pai, founding partner of 3one4 Capital, gave Karnataka’s innovation story a distinctly Namma Bengaluru touch.The Bengaluru-Karnataka startup ecosystem is valued at $153 billion, having grown 190% over the second half of 2018-20. It attracted $39 billion in venture capital funding between 2021 and 2025 and accounts for about 46% of India’s startup VC raised since 2010, according to Bengaluru Innovation Report 2026 brought out in association with Karnataka govt, 3one4 Capital, KDEM and Startup Karnataka.The report also highlights Karnataka’s growing AI credentials. Bengaluru ranks second in Asia among AI-native startup clusters. AI startups in the ecosystem have raised about $1.5 billion since 2020, including more than $1.2 billion for application-layer AI. The AI-native ecosystem is valued at $2 billion and has grown 109%, with the region accounting for 58% of India’s AI startup funding.The ecosystem has around 300 venture capital firms and 30 active unicorns. It recorded 304 startup exits between 2021 and 2025, with a combined exit value of $46 billion.Pai said Karnataka ranked second in the country in the number of alternative investment funds (AIFs) or venture capital funds, based on Sebi data. It was also second in Asia in the number of AI-native startups and second in the country in GST collections. “One criticism often levelled at startups is that they do not pay enough tax. This report shows how much tax we generate, not just through business income but also through GST and capital gains,” he said.The report’s innovation figures sit alongside Karnataka’s significant contribution to the national exchequer. The state contributed Rs 1.5 lakh crore in domestic goods and services tax (GST) in 2025-26, accounting for 9.7% of India’s total collections. Its net direct tax contribution stood at Rs 2.62 lakh crore in 2024-25, or 12% of the national total.Karnataka ranked second nationally in both categories, behind Maharashtra, which collected Rs 3.6 lakh crore in GST in 2025-26 and Rs 8.9 lakh crore in net direct taxes in 2024-25. Karnataka’s GST collections were higher than Gujarat’s Rs 1.3 lakh crore and Tamil Nadu’s Rs 1.3 lakh crore. Its direct tax contribution was also ahead of Delhi, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat and Telangana.The figures underline Karnataka’s position as one of the country’s largest economic and tax contributors.The report identifies six clusters — Mysuru, Mangaluru, Hubballi-Dharwad-Belagavi, Kalaburagi, Shivamogga and Tumakuru — as key to expanding the digital economy beyond Bengaluru.Mysuru’s gross district domestic product (GDDP) is estimated at Rs 88,717 crore, or 3.4% of the state’s economy. The cluster has more than 450 startups, over 20,000 IT professionals and annual IT exports of Rs 5,700 crore. Mangaluru has a GDDP of Rs 1.3 lakh crore, accounting for 5.3% of the state economy, with more than 500 startups and 250 technology companies.Infrastructure expansion is also underway. Mangaluru has five IT parks with 10 lakh sq ft of office space under construction, while its Derebail IT Park is a Rs 135-crore project expected to support 11,000 jobs. In Mysuru, the Rs 245.67-crore Electronics Manufacturing Cluster at Kochanahalli is spread across 235.5 acres. A 150-acre printed circuit board park has also been announced.The state’s Local Economy Accelerator Programme (LEAP) is a five-year, Rs 1,000-crore initiative aimed at generating five lakh jobs and setting up six new Centres of Excellence. It includes investments in agri-tech and rural innovation in Kalaburagi, quantum computing and AI in Dharwad, and an AI centre at IIIT Raichur.Karnataka has also supported 1,479 startups through its Elevate programme since 2017, committing grants worth Rs 393 crore. Of these, 571 winners were from districts outside Bengaluru.Karnataka Startup Policy 2025-30 targets 25,000 additional startups, including 10,000 from Beyond Bengaluru clusters.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Medicare out-of-pocket costs are rising in 2027
articles.summary: Medicare Part B premiums and deductibles will jump in 2027, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services announced Tuesday.
articles.body:
Medicare, which provides health insurance coverage to roughly 75 million retired seniors and disabled workers in the US, is getting more expensive next year.

Medicare Part B premiums, which cover doctors, outpatient care, some home healthcare services, and durable medical equipment, will rise about 3.2% to $209.40 a month in 2027, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) announced Tuesday .

That's an increase of $6.50 a month from $202.90 in 2026, bringing the total premium to $2,512.80 a year.

The Medicare Part B premium is deducted from your Social Security checks before you receive them. The Social Security Administration announced a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) for 2027 . Starting in January, the increase will add an average of $75 per month.

That is great news, but the Medicare premium increase will eat into it.

The annual deductible for all Medicare Part B beneficiaries increases to $292 in 2027, up $9 from $283 in 2026.

The increase in the standard premium and deductible is mainly due to projected increases in healthcare spending, according to CMS.

"The increase in the Medicare Part B premium for 2027 is less than the much steeper 10% increase in 2026, so that's a bit of good news," said Juliette Cubanski, director of the program on Medicare policy at KFF.

"Still, this increase comes on top of rising costs for other Medicare benefits, including prescription drugs, plus rising costs for other everyday essentials," she added.

People with traditional Medicare generally pay the Part B premium for physician coverage and a separate one for prescription drug coverage, known as Part D. Those premiums vary by plan. Some people pay an additional monthly premium for inpatient hospital coverage (Part A).

Each year, the Medicare Part B premium, deductible, and coinsurance rates are reset. If you're enrolled in traditional Medicare, you also have a Part D drug plan. The 2027 Part D base premium is $36 per month on average, but yours could be higher.

"Americans clearly understand that healthcare costs can threaten their retirement security," Kelly LaVigne, vice president of Consumer Insights at Allianz Life, told Yahoo Finance. But "so many don't fully understand what Medicare will and won't cover. And the details matter."

Roughly 15% of the average retiree's annual expenses will be health-related, according to Fidelity. On average, a 65-year-old who leaves the workforce this year may need $185,500 in savings to cover out-of-pocket healthcare expenses throughout retirement.

articles.title: Gonzalo Bernardos, economista, y la dictadura de Franco: "Hizo que durante 20 años la miseria se propagara en España"
articles.standfirst: El profesor universitario analiza el impacto de la dictadura en el país
articles.summary: El profesor universitario analiza el impacto de la dictadura en el país
articles.body: Gonzalo Bernardos, economista, ha analizado el impacto del franquismo en el desarrollo de nuestro país. "La dictadura de Franco hizo que durante 20 años la miseria se propagara en España", ha afirmado en sus redes sociales. El profesor universitario ha señalado, además, que el ritmo al que avanzó el territorio no tuvo nada que ver con el que experimentaron otras zonas del viejo continente: "Mientras la mayor parte del resto de Europa Occidental progresaba mucho". Gonzalo Bernardos ha compartido, además, un vídeo titulado 'Así se vivía en la España de los años 50' y ha realizado la siguiente reflexión: "Dedicado a todos aquellos que dicen que ahora dicen se vive muy mal. Yo no he vivido los años 50 del siglo pasado, pero sí me lo han contado mis padres". El economista ha explicado que familia no guardó, precisamente, un buen recuerdo de esa época. "Fueron años de gran miseria. Incluso había racionamiento. Con el plan de estabilización empezó el progreso", ha afirmado el economista sobre la dictadura franquista. En el vídeo compartido por Gonzalo Bernardos se expone lo siguiente: "No era una vida mejor. Había más frío, más hambre y más miedo a enfermar, y no todas las familias lo pasaron igual. Pero quien la vivió no la ha olvidado". La Ley 20/2022, de 19 de octubre, de Memoria Democrática, en su preámbulo, informa lo siguiente sobre la dictadura franquista: "Los hechos descritos por el Consejo de Europa señalan que durante la Guerra de España se cometieron gravísimos crímenes y que durante la posterior dictadura franquista se estableció un sistema político autoritario que reprimió masivamente todo atisbo de oposición política de manera sistemática y generalizada. Como indica el referido informe del Consejo de Europa, en España se produjeron de manera sistemática desapariciones forzadas, ejecuciones extrajudiciales, detenciones arbitrarias, políticas de campos de concentración, trabajos forzados, torturas, violaciones e incluso secuestro masivo de recién nacidos bajo una política de inspiración eugenésica".

articles.title: Home contract signings hit multidecade low as buyers struggle with high rates and prices
articles.summary: Home contract signings are the lowest since at least 2001.
articles.body:
Home contract signings dropped to a record low as prospective buyers fled a market where both prices and mortgage rates have remained elevated.

The Pending Home Sales Index, which measures contract activity, dropped 4.7% from September to October and nearly 17% from a year ago to reach the lowest level since at least 2001, according to new data from the National Association of Realtors.

Economists surveyed by Bloomberg had been expecting a smaller 14.5% year-over-year drop and a 2% monthly decline. Mortgage rates climbed above 7% in September and remained elevated in October, further freezing an already slow-moving market.

Homes typically go under contract a month or two before they're sold, making pending home sales an early indicator of future sales activity. Recent weakness in home sales and contract activity means 2026 is on track to be the worst year for home sales in over 30 years.

Existing home sales dropped 5.5% in October from a month earlier and 8.8% from October 2025 to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of just 3.75 million homes, according to NAR data. Sales haven't been that slow since August 2010, when the housing market was still recovering from the aftermath of the 2008 financial crisis.

Homebuilders are feeling it too. US homebuilder confidence fell to its lowest level in more than 14 years in November, and 46% of builders reported cutting prices to lure more buyers.

At the heart of the gridlock are high mortgage rates, which averaged 6.38% at this time last year but are now closer to 7.5%.

"Affordability remains the limiting factor in today's housing market," Realtor.com senior economist Hannah Jones said in a statement.

Claire Boston is a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

articles.title: Why Nvidia doesn't need a 'big splashy hire' to replace Jensen Huang as CEO
articles.summary: Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and "Shark Tank" star Kevin O'Leary make a great point on the Nvidia leadership drama.
articles.body:
Maybe Nvidia ( NVDA ) doesn't need a big free-agent CEO signing to replace highly visible founder and former CEO Jensen Huang.

"If you don't bring Jensen back, I would not hire an outsider," Amazon ( AMZN ) founder and former CEO Jeff Bezos said at a Semafor conference on Tuesday. "Nvidia is too complicated. I think outside CEOs in complex companies have a vanishingly small chance of succeeding."

A new CEO often comes in and runs the standard playbook from an MBA class: Do a listening tour with employees to better understand the business. Meet with the existing C-suite to see who they want to keep and who should get pushed out.

Six months into the job, the new CEO unveils a splashy growth plan that often includes profit-boosting layoffs.

The thing is, Nvidia doesn't need any of this playbook inserted into its unique culture Huang created. It also doesn't need its important operations disrupted by a meddling new CEO seeking praise from the world.

At best, Nvidia needs an internal CEO hire — someone with Huang's technical prowess who could sell the sizzle to a global audience.

At worst, it needs a big-name veteran CEO who promises the board no major overhauls, just small tweaks where needed. That person stays in the job for a few years and establishes a strong succession plan — one that Huang never whipped up.

For his part, Bezos and his board named then-AWS leader and longtime Amazon exec Andy Jassy to succeed him as CEO in 2021.

"I don't think it needs a big splashy hire. I think they have incredible bench strength in there," investor and "Shark Tank" star Kevin O'Leary said on Sozzi Unleashed . "I think they have a tremendous amount of engineers designing the next two generations of chips. I think it's a machine unto itself right now."

Nvidia CEO Huang resigns amid affair scandals

Who is Colette Kress, Nvidia's new interim CEO?

3 challenges for a post-Jensen Huang Nvidia

Interim CEO Colette Kress made a solid case late Tuesday for staying in the interim CEO role for perhaps longer than Wall Street expects. The company's third quarter was solid , the outlook strong, and Kress came across as a steady hand driving the Nvidia rocketship.

For the third quarter, Nvidia posted adjusted earnings of $2.68 a share on revenue of $115.8 billion. Wall Street had expected earnings of $2.47 a share on revenue of $109.15 billion.

Nvidia expects fourth quarter revenue of $127.4 billion to $132.6 billion, comfortably above the $125.25 billion analysts were looking for.

The company said it sees fiscal year 2028 revenue growth of 75%, up from a prior estimate of 70% offered just three months ago.

articles.title: El SEPE permite cobrar el paro a los trabajadores en excedencia si pierden un segundo empleo
articles.standfirst: Estas son las especificaciones que debes conocer
articles.summary: Estas son las especificaciones que debes conocer
articles.body: El SEPE (Servicio Público de Empleo Estatal) concede la prestación por desempleo a los trabajadores en excedencia voluntaria si pierden un segundo empleo por causas ajenas a su voluntad, tal y como ha confirmado María José Gómez, asesora de la subdirección de Prestaciones en su intervención en el programa de Telemadrid 'Madrid Trabaja'. "Si tienes una situación legal de desempleo en otra empresa porque has trabajado en otra empresa mientras tenías esa excedencia y has finalizado una relación laboral de forma no voluntaria tú podrás solicitar una prestación por desempleo en función de esa situación que se ha generado al terminar el trabajo", ha apuntado la asesora. De esta manera, aunque pedir una excedencia por iniciativa propia no da derecho directo a cobrar el paro, trabajar para otra empresa durante ese periodo y sufrir un despido o fin de contrato genera una nueva situación legal de desempleo, por lo que permite acceder a la ayuda. Tal como detalla la guía del SEPE sobre excedencia voluntaria, hay que tener en cuenta varias especificaciones. Si la excedencia aún no ha terminado, puedes solicitar y cobrar el paro sin necesidad de pedir el reingreso previo en tu empresa original; en cambio, si la prestación dura más que el tiempo restante de excedencia, el pago se suspenderá en la fecha exacta en que finalice dicha excedencia. En caso de que la excedencia finalice mientras cobras el paro, debes solicitar la reincorporación a tu empresa de origen. Si la empresa te deniega el reingreso por falta de vacantes, podrás reanudar el cobro de la prestación presentando su respuesta. Finalmente, si la excedencia ya había terminado al perder el segundo empleo, deberás pedir primero el reingreso en tu empresa original. Solo si te confirman que no hay plazas disponibles podrás tramitar la prestación por desempleo.

articles.title: Largest US egg producer to cull 1.8 million birds after bird flu outbreak
articles.summary: Cal-Maine reports avian influenza at Florida site, with 2.7 percent of its total flock affected.
articles.body:
Cal-Maine Foods, the largest egg producer in the United States, has said it would cull 1.8 million birds after avian influenza was detected at one of its facilities in Florida.

On Wednesday, the company said the 1.4 million laying hens and 360,000 young hens being culled account for 2.7 percent of its flock. Production at the facility will be temporarily halted.

Cal-Maine said in a statement that it would coordinate with other production and distribution facilities to minimise disruption across the company.

The risk bird flu poses to human health is low. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), there have been 74 human cases since February 2024, with no evidence of human-to-human transmission.

However, the virus continues to pose a significant challenge to the US poultry and egg industries. Some 21.5 million birds have been affected this year, following a historic surge in outbreaks in late 2024 and early 2025 that sharply reduced the number of egg-laying hens.

Approximately 50.7 million laying hens were lost between mid-October 2024 and early March 2025, when egg prices in the US reached a record high of $6.23 per dozen.

The current average retail price of eggs is $2.32 per dozen, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

Despite the announcement that production at the Florida facility would be temporarily halted, Cal-Maine’s stock rose 5.3 percent in early trading.

articles.title: Waymo pulls robotaxis off highways after California ban, with tech seen as 'far from perfect'
articles.summary: The robotaxi rollout in America hit a roadblock.
articles.body:
The robotaxi rollout in America hit a roadblock.

Alphabet-owned ( GOOGL ) Waymo pulled its robotaxis off freeways in every US market where it offers them, after California regulators banned the company's driverless cars from state highways.

The move comes as Waymo races to scale its ride-hailing business, where freeway rides are key to growth.

The California Department of Motor Vehicles imposed the restrictions on Nov. 11, though they weren't made public until Tuesday. The agency said Waymo's driverless freeway operations pose an "imminent hazard to public safety," citing "recurring incursions" by its vehicles into active construction zones, per the AP .

According to the DMV, three Waymo vehicles entered an active construction zone on US Highway 101 near Burlingame. In a separate incident, video showed a Waymo trying to pass two California Highway Patrol cruisers on Interstate 280 in San Francisco while officers slowed traffic to clear debris. Waymo said the Highway 101 encounters caused no injuries or collisions.

The ban stays in place until Waymo shows the DMV "effective corrective actions."

A Waymo spokesperson said the company had "temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance." That includes Phoenix, where Waymo launched freeway rides last November alongside San Francisco and Los Angeles.

Yahoo Finance reached out to Waymo for comment but did not immediately hear back.

It's not the first time Waymo pulled service from the highway. In May, seven of its robotaxis drove into active freeway construction lanes in the Bay Area, following similar events in Phoenix in April. Waymo pulled its fleet off freeways and filed a voluntary software recall covering nearly 3,900 vehicles before freeway rides resumed.

Waymo's street coverage is unaffected. Waymo says it handles more than half a million trips a week across 15 US cities, and the map keeps growing.

Last month, Waymo added nearly 250 square miles of service across five cities, including Torrance in Los Angeles, La Jolla in San Diego, and a connection to BART's Berryessa Station in the Bay Area. It also opened rides to everyone in San Antonio, San Diego, and Tampa, and added pickups at Las Vegas' Harry Reid International Airport for existing riders.

Tesla ( TSLA ) expanded its robotaxi service in Miami recently, as well as Austin .

But the freeway pullback shows that regulators, not companies like Waymo, set the pace of the robotaxi rollout.

"Local regulation is the biggest barrier right now, but that's a good thing," Anthony Townsend, senior research associate at Cornell Tech and author of "Ghost Road: Beyond the Driverless Car," said to Yahoo Finance. "This technology is far from perfect, and right now it's mostly a tool for perpetuating auto dependency."
